card.name: Subject noun before an outcome verb
card.fires_on: The noun that ends the subject of a sentence, such as cases, events, therapy or edema, right before a verb stating what happened. It is most common after 'Some of these' or 'Some' in adverse-reaction text.

modes.label: Some of these cases/events
modes.description: Plural noun or 'which' after 'Some (of these)' just before a verb like resulted or have been fatal.
modes.example: Some of these reported<< cases>> resulted in fatalities or liver transplantation.

modes.label: Treatment or condition as subject
modes.description: A therapy or condition noun that is the subject, followed by a verb describing an outcome.
modes.example: initiation of octreotide acetate injection<< therapy>> resulted in worsening of CHF

modes.label: Non-drug subject
modes.description: A subject noun in general web text, followed by a verb describing a consequence.
modes.example: lost part of its tax-exempt<< status>> because it refused

card.writes: It favors verbs that report what actually happened (finally, did also, carried out) and disfavors conditional or modal words like if, can, must.
card.plain: It fires on the subject noun just before the sentence says what happened as a result, as in 'Some of these cases resulted in...'.
evidence: Some of these reported<< cases>> resulted in fatalities or liver transplantation.
Some of these<< events>> have been fatal or life-threatening.
some of<< which>> resulted in hospitalization.
